blueprint.pageTitle: Manage Engine Endpoint Central | Unified Endpoint Management & Security
blueprint.metaDescription: Centralize endpoint management, security, patching, compliance, and remote support with Manage Engine Endpoint Central. Built for IT teams that need control, visibility, and operational confidence.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark split gradient with subtle grid lines, glow edges, and floating endpoint-status chips
sections.designNote: Use a content-first split hero that answers what it is, who it is for, and what to do next. Left side: strong headline, concise supporting copy, one orange CTA labeled Get started, and a compact 3-bullet value stack. Right side: layered browser-frame dashboard visual showing device inventory, patch status, compliance score, and remote support widgets. Keep the hero authoritative and operational, not promotional.

Place trust immediately after the hero using 3-6 recognizable enterprise/customer logos if available; if not, use a slim metric strip with counts for endpoints managed, patch coverage, and compliance readiness. Keep it compact, horizontally aligned, and visually restrained.

Make the first product block the main explanation zone. Use a large spotlight panel for Patch & Update Management paired with a preview dashboard frame, then a 2x2 supporting grid for Browser Security, Data Security, and Vulnerability Remediation. The second product block should switch to split-panel-list format with alternating text and small UI panels for Strengthen Endpoint Security, Manage IT Assets Effectively, Enhance Application Control & Privileges, Facilitate Remote Access & Troubleshooting, and Ensure Compliance. Keep the section technical, scan-friendly, and visually dense without becoming crowded.

Insert a 3-step how-it-works section under 60 seconds to match warm traffic expectations. Use a numbered workflow canvas: discover endpoints, automate patch/security actions, then monitor and respond from one console. Pair the steps with a compact operational timeline or command-center style diagram. This section should feel instructional and reduce implementation anxiety.

Use proof after workflow as credibility reinforcement. Show 3-5 enterprise testimonial cards with the most relevant roles highlighted, and present each as a polished validation card with quote, name, designation, and subtle company/role emphasis. Avoid a carousel unless space forces it; a clean 2-row card grid is more stable and trust-building for this audience.

Turn the remaining value into role-based use cases for IT teams, Service Desk Administrators, Infrastructure Managers, Operations Managers, and Senior System Administrators. Use alternating left-right panels with mini dashboard fragments, compliance callouts, and device-management snapshots. Focus on operational confidence, audit readiness, and reduced support load.

Close with a decisive conversion block using a floating card over a subtle dark field. Keep the headline short, the form compact, and the primary CTA strictly Get started in solid orange at 100% opacity. The visual should feel like a secure handoff from exploration to action, not a salesy form wall.

blueprint.designPersonality: Disciplined, technical, and enterprise-assured. The page should feel like a secure control center for modern IT teams: dark, structured, highly legible, and credibility-first, with orange acting as the decisive action color and logos serving as the primary trust mechanism.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use polished endpoint management dashboard-style visuals inside designed frames only: browser frames, dashboard cards, workflow canvases, and bento panels. Include device inventory, patch status tiles, compliance indicators, vulnerability alerts, and remote support widgets. If any logo or screenshot media is used, ensure it belongs to the current product or is a valid customer/logo trust asset. No raw screenshots as full-width sections.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and descriptive, so 48px keeps it strong without wrapping awkwardly on desktop.

colours.colourReason: The product is security-focused, so the palette uses a dark navy authority base with the brand's orange as the primary action and emphasis color. This preserves trust, visibility, and a clear CTA hierarchy while staying aligned to Techjockey brand colors.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Full-width top hero with brand/logo anchoring on one side, bold headline stack, short supporting copy, and a compact benefit list using icon+text bullets. The hero is text-forward and conversion-oriented rather than image-led.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column landing-page flow with a hero, lead form block, then feature sections. Content is arranged in stacked sections with clear separation, minimal nesting, and a straightforward scan path.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple utility-style cards/blocks with strong borders or subtle depth, limited decorative treatment, and utility-first spacing. Feature items read as compact text cards rather than rich media cards.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears as a single dominant action in the hero and is repeated as a lead-generation form context rather than multiple competing buttons. Secondary CTA is absent or de-emphasized.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not present in the provided reference snippet.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage; logo image in hero and icon bullets. No hero illustration, product screenshot, or media panel dominant in the visible structure.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Feature-led content sections with headline, short descriptive intro, and multi-item benefit lists. Layout favors grouped bullet/card items in a grid or stacked list, with clear section headers and concise explanatory copy.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead-capture form block placed immediately after the hero, visually separated as a distinct card section. Form is structured for conversion with hidden metadata fields and a prominent section headline.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, low-motion presentation with no visible animated transitions in the provided markup.
designNotes: Prioritize clarity and lead conversion over storytelling visuals.
Use a strong top-to-bottom hierarchy: brand, headline, benefits, form, features.
Keep feature modules concise and scannable with limited decorative complexity.
Use generous whitespace to separate major blocks and reduce cognitive load.
Avoid dependency on carousels, tabs, or interactive reveals for core information delivery.

blueprint.heroFormBgRule: MANDATORY: Use heroBackgroundVideo as full-bleed autoplay muted loop video behind everything

mustHaveMoments: Sticky top banner with logo anchoring and persistent trust strip
Hero with strong product value proposition and single dominant Request Demo CTA
Logo-first trust band placed high on the page to satisfy credibility expectations
Dedicated lead-capture form block immediately after the hero if form is required
Feature-led sections with concise utility cards for patching, security, compliance, and remote management
Testimonial section focused on IT operations and infrastructure roles
Clear section headings that preserve the provided content hierarchy and terminology
avoidPatterns: Do not use hero-right imagery if a form is placed in the hero area
Do not leave empty space or underbuild the page below the hero
Do not introduce unsupported pricing, tabs, accordions, or carousel behavior
Do not rely on generic stock-style visuals that dilute the enterprise IT theme
Do not make testimonials or feature content visually heavier than the primary conversion path
Do not mismatch content by rephrasing the product into a generic endpoint or cybersecurity page
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is for a single product and the goal is demo booking for a solution-aware IT audience, so the best strategy is a product-led conversion flow with strong credibility upfront. Because the user specifically says logos are the dominant trust signal, the design should prioritize logo visibility early, ideally in a sticky top strip and near the hero. The content is medium-volume and enterprise-focused, so a balanced layout with a split hero, clear supporting copy, and stacked feature sections will keep scanning easy without feeling sparse. The message should stay confident and efficient, with a strong CTA and minimal distraction. Testimonials should reinforce operational value for IT roles, while the overall page should remain clean, professional, and conversion-oriented.
